messages:

Soojin,

We started seeing widespread 429s and 2-3s tail latency on our payment scoring calls starting ~10:00 PT this morning. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on our side; QPS is within our agreed limits. Examples attached in the body (request ids). This is impacting checkout flows for ~15% of sessions.

Sample 429 header: x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-burst-remaining: 12, x-plan: standard

Can you triage? We are open to a temporary lift while you investigate.

- Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 429s — initial triage

On Thu, Mar 9, 2028 at 8:30 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Samir — thanks for the quick heads-up...

Quick initial findings from the request traces + control plane:
- We see a flurry of 429s sourced from the customer's API key between 10:00-10:45 PT.
- Rate-limit response headers indicate the customer is tagged as `plan=standard` with a burst allowance of 50. Their historical peak burst has been ~350.
- Routing logs show their traffic was routed through the hosted shared tier (policy id: policy-shared-v2) instead of their Dedicated pool (dedicated-acme-01).

Hypothesis: A recent policy rollout incorrectly matched their org-id to a default shared policy; that lowered their burst allowance and caused prefix backpressure + elevated tail latency (requests spent more time queueing).

Attaching trace sample and compressed logs for the 10:12:xx window.
Attachments: debug-trace-logs.zip (request ids 7c1f.., 7c2b.. included)

I'll try a config patch to pin their org-id to the dedicated route as a test (non-disruptive) and report back.

— Marcus (SRE)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Mar 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 429s — policy mis-tagging found

On Thu, Mar 9, 2028 at 9:02 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick initial findings from the request traces + control plane:

Confirmed: a policy rollout yesterday added a permissive matching rule that accidentally matched org metadata for Acme (org-acme-prod) to the `policy-shared-v2` bucket. The matching priority fell through; previously they had an explicit pin to `dedicated-acme-01`.

Mitigation action taken (10:07 PT):
- Pushed a temporary override to pin org-acme-prod back to dedicated-acme-01 (non-rolling change).
- Temporarily bumped burst allowance to 500 to drain queued requests.
- Monitoring dashboards show 429s dropping after 10:20 PT and tail latency improving by ~70% within 12 minutes.

Permanent next steps: roll a fix to the policy matcher to add stricter org-id anchoring and add an integration test to the policy rollout pipeline.

I've attached the policy diff for the temporary override (policy-change.diff).

Samir — apologies for the impact. We kept a short timeline for the mitigation; please confirm whether you're still seeing errors or any degraded throughput.

— Stephanie (Policy & Routing)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden latency and 429s — executive attention requested

FYI / Marissa & Laura — putting this on your radar. Acme (large ecommerce payments customer, DEAL-4891) experienced production throttling due to a policy rollout that mis-tagged their org and routed traffic to shared capacity with a much lower burst allowance.

Impact: ~15% checkout failures for ~45 minutes; business reported increased cart abandonment. Mitigation: temporary pin to dedicated pool + burst bump; errors decreased and latency improved.

Proposed executive actions for approval:
- Approve one week of service credit (requested by CSM) as a goodwill gesture and to avoid churn.
- Prioritize a post-mortem and policy rollout gate (integration test) to prevent recurrence.

I've included the debugging artifacts (debug-trace-logs.zip) and policy change diff.

— Soojin
